page.layout: One printed page. At the top: page number at left, running head centred. Below that: two round portrait medallions side by side, with legends around their rims. Below them: one full-width text column with two paragraphs, the first on Henry VIII and the second on Edward VI. No margin notes. No catchword or signature.

main_text.l: HENRIC[?] ANG. R.[?]
D. ADOAR
R. ANG.
HENRICVS octauus, Angliæ Rex, patri Henrico septi-
mo successit in Regno, anno Christi 1510. Qui traiecto in Gal-
liam exercitu, Neruiorum vrbem Tornacum certis conditio-
nibus recepit: quam quinque post annis Francisco Valesio Re-
gi restituit, pactus filiæ suæ Mariæ connubium, cum Francisco
Franciæ Delphino. Postea vero anno 1520. in Galliam reuersus
visendi gratia Regis Francisci, pacem cum eo firmauit. Tragœ-
dias vero turbulētissimas[?] quas excitauit, quásque[?] sævitias exer-
cuit, & in Clerum, & in suas vxores, nunc commemorare non
libet: qui fusius hæc videre volet, legat Iouij primum, & secun-
dum tomum, & Supplementum Chronicorum. Regnauit an-
nos 36. & mortuus est anno 1546.
EDVARDVS sextus, Angliæ Rex supradicti Henrici fi-
lius, annos natus octo patri successit, anno mundi 5508. & à
Christo nato 1546. Hic puer fuisse dicitur (quantum tulit ætas)
multum eruditus, ac pius: pacis amantissimus, & animo ad tran-
quillitatem inclinato. Bononiam maritimam Henrico 2. Regi
Franciæ reddidit, annos quinque prius occupatâ à patre Henrico
octauo. Inter eos denique post grauissima bella de pace
conuentum[?] est, iis legibus, vt odiorum veterum inter Gallos, &
Britannos[?] perpetua fieret amnestia: idque omnium Magna-
tum consensu, & populi diutinorum bellorum vtrinque pertæsi.
Quasanè[?] pax, & concordia omnibus fuit quàm gratissima.
Vide Chronica Franciæ[?], & Iouium.

page.notes: The medallion legends are printed on the woodcut, not in the text. The left one reads roughly "HENRIC[?] ANG. R."; a small "P G" also appears on the left medallion, faint. The right medallion reads "D. ADOAR" and "R. ANG.". Letters on the rims are partly worn; I have marked the doubtful parts with [?]. The lower part of the second paragraph is faint and blurred (around "conuentum", "Britannos", "Quasanè", "Vide Chronica"), so those readings are doubtful. The first word of the second paragraph and the numbers 1510, 1520, 5508 and 1546 were read with some care because the type is worn.
